item.description: The Financial Times says computing giant Nvidia has approached Rene Haas, CEO of British chip designer Arm, in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang. Huang resigned after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Meanwhile some employees are clamouring for Huang's return – as his fellow tech leader Elon Musk. Campaign groups, students and Yellow Vest protesters are due to join forces in the capital, bringing together demands on wages, education and civil liberties. But after weeks of demonstrations, union leaders warn that protest fatigue is setting in, while police officers are seeking better compensation for the risk of policing the protests. item.title: US nationwide flight ground stop: "Our routers got overloaded with data"
item.description: On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop. More than 8,200 flights, or over 31% of those scheduled in the United States, were canceled. The ground stop lasted nearly five hours and was the longest in the country since September 11, 2001. Officials blamed outdated air traffic communications equipment, and said that there was no evidence of a cyber attack. The airspace is now reopened and flights have resumed. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: La gestión de los recursos para la reconstrucción tras el terremoto enfrenta nuevas críticas. Este viernes renunció el gerente del Fondo Milagro, entidad creada para administrar los recursos destinados a la emergencia, en medio de cuestionamientos por su gestión. La polémica se intensificó tras conocerse los altos salarios de algunos funcionarios y las denuncias sobre el lento avance de las obras. Legisladores señalaron que, más de tres meses después de la catástrofe, el fondo solo había firmado unos pocos contratos para demolición, mientras miles de afectados siguen esperando soluciones.
